syntax: NTH_VALUE(value, n) OVER (PARTITION BY team ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
summary: NTH_VALUE returns the expression from the nth row of the current window frame, counting from one.
documentation: NTH_VALUE returns the expression from the nth row of the current window frame, counting from one. A full-partition frame can repeat a selected observation beside every row, and a missing nth row produces NULL.
inputs: readings(id INTEGER, team TEXT NOT NULL, value INTEGER), with distinct ids.
returns: id, team and second_value, ordered by team then id.
caution: The chosen row follows the window ordering, not numeric value order. A NULL value in an existing second row stays NULL, just like a missing second row.
scenarios: Repeat a second baseline observation beside later readings.
Attach a chosen ordered checkpoint to each row in a report.
Compare records with a fixed position in their local group.
title: Repeat the second observation
problem: For every row, return id, team and the second value by ascending id within its team AS second_value. Use a full-partition ROWS frame and order output by team, id.
hint: Pass 2 to NTH_VALUE and end the frame at UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING.
goal: Use NTH_VALUE() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
